findings.text: The commit changes how `merged_search_path` groups trusted and candidate packages and which file each merged link points to. It now checks letter case in each original root, adds alias links, and picks a file from any root where the name resolves, and `migration_check/prepare.py:66` uses the result for export and replay, so owner review required. The rule also has a gap: `case_aliases` is one shared set keyed by `casefold`, so if a case-insensitive candidate root has `belay` and a case-sensitive trusted root has `Belay`, the two are merged anyway. Then the import `belay.Foo` resolves to the trusted `Belay/Foo.olean`, but with the original roots it resolves to the candidate's `belay/Foo.olean`. That breaks the docstring's promise that names follow each original root's case rules. Fix: have the owner review the new grouping and file selection, and merge two spellings only when the root that holds each one treats them as the same name.

The commit changes behavior with no test that would fail without it. It adds alias links for each original spelling, checks letter case in each root instead of in the workspace, and selects files from every root where the name resolves, but `tests/test_import_path.py` is unchanged. Fix: add a deterministic test for a case-sensitive workspace with case-insensitive roots, for example by replacing the case check with a stub. It must check that the alias links exist and that the first root still wins.
